By department: Homelessness and Supportive Housing $6,371,410; Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development $6,061,473; Human Rights Commission $3,695,140; Status of Women $1,407,270; Public Health $1,277,342; Economic & Workforce Development $583,754. The table of every payment has $19,260,329 for the same years, $136,060 less; $136,061 of that is in fiscal 2023 at Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development. The nonprofit-spending table prints the payee as “St James Infirmary” and the table of every payment as “ST JAMES INFIRMARY”. Each organization's payments in the two tables the Controller publishes, as retrieved on 12 November 2026: Citywide Nonprofit Spending, which by its own description keeps contracted services only, and Vendor Payments (Vouchers), the table of every payment. The fiscal year is the one printed on the payment. Payee names are matched by the rule the organization pages use: the name without punctuation and company suffixes, plus the renames and spellings that a shared contract number confirms.
tables.limits: A payment is money the City sent, not money the organization kept or spent on itself: subsidies, rent aid and grants that an organization pays on to others are in these figures. The two tables differ where the nonprofit-spending table leaves out a kind of payment or a contract; neither is wrong for that reason. The year printed on a payment can be later than the year the payment was issued. A payee the City spells in a way that no contract number ties to the organization is not counted.

tables.how: 33 contract numbers, agreed at $26,804,269 together. The largest is the grant the case describes, number 1000024043, “St James - Bryant Nav Center”, 2021-12-01 to 2024-06-30: $8,964,393 agreed and $6,371,409 paid, recorded as “Grants only - no bid - emergency procurement”. Counted by the rule recorded: 21 another rule (most often a grant made under grant-making authority); 9 competitively bid; 3 not bid: an emergency, sole-source or standing waiver rule. 8 of the agreements are titled for another group (TGI Justice Project, TAJA's Coalition, the Transgender District, Compton's Transgender Cultural District) or say “fiscal sponsor”: a fiscal sponsor receives and administers a grant on behalf of another group. Every contract number in the City's Supplier Contracts table, as retrieved on 12 November 2026, whose prime contractor is the organization; the agreed and paid amounts add every member of the contract's team.
tables.limits: The table holds no record of whether other operators were asked before the navigation-center grant was made, or of why the emergency rule was used. Money received as a sponsor for another group is that group's to spend, so part of what was paid to this organization was not for its own programs; the table does not say how much. The table shows a contract's present amount and keeps no history, so it cannot show what was first signed or how often it was amended. A purchasing rule that says a contract was not bid is the City’s own rule for that kind of grant or service, not a finding. Payments under a contract are also in the payment lists; the two must not be added.

tables.how: From each of the organization's 5 returns on file (years ending June 2021 to June 2025). For the year ending 30 June 2024: net assets at the start $5,923,529, plus revenue less expenses $68,843, plus other changes reported $0, gives $5,992,372; the return reports $204,560 at the end; $5,787,812 is on no line. The same sum for the other years leaves: year ending June 2021, nothing; year ending June 2022, nothing; year ending June 2023, nothing; year ending June 2025, nothing. The returns for the years ending June 2021 ($-415,768) and June 2022 ($87,887) come out only because each carries a prior-period adjustment of that amount; the return for June 2024 carries none. The short form for the year ending June 2025 opens at $0 although the return before it closed at $204,560. The lines of Part XI that are marked “not filled in” are absent from the return's file. The returns give the filer's name as “ST JAMES INFIRMARY”; they are one organization's by their employer identification number, 94-3330568.
tables.limits: A difference between two lines of a return is not money missing. The most likely reading, which the case gives, is that grants were booked as income when awarded, never collected in full, and dropped from the balance sheet at closure without a write-off line; in that case earlier income was overstated on paper and no cash left. Only the organization's own books or its preparer's workpapers can say. A tax return is the organization's own statement, signed under penalty of perjury and not audited by the IRS. Its tax year is often not the City's fiscal year, and it counts money when earned or spent under its accounting method, not when the City paid. A disclosure on a return, including a dealing with an officer or a director, is what the law requires to be reported; the question is whether it is fair and approved.

tables.limits: Two organizations paying each other can be what fiscal sponsorship looks like: a sponsor receives a group's grants, pays its staff and passes money on, and the group repays shared costs. The agreement titles and the tax number on another giver's return point to that arrangement here, but no document on file states it. Only organizations whose returns were collected for this project can appear as givers, so grants from foundations and other funders are missing. A tax return is the organization's own statement, signed under penalty of perjury and not audited by the IRS. tables.how: The board's complete list, as retrieved on 13 November 2026, searched for the organization's name: 1 entry, dated 2024-04-02. The list gives a name, a city and the board's own entity number, and no federal tax number.
tables.limits: The match is by name and city only and is not confirmed: another entity of the same name could be the one listed. The list does not say why an exemption was revoked, and an entry is not a finding about how an organization was run.
